title: JZ-motion: explainers, fast (about this app, with edit demo)

elements.text: an LLM-first studio for explainer videos

beats.title: Logo
beats.notes: Hi, it's Jakub here. Today I will share with you my latest app, jz-motion.

beats.title: What it is
beats.notes: This is an LLM-first explainer video creator. Everything you will see here was produced by it, including the glowing marker board, animations, text and charts.

beats.title: The usual tools
beats.notes: No Photoshop, After Effects or Premiere.

beats.title: What I use instead
beats.notes: Just me, Claude Code and my application.

elements.text:
what if the board
drew itself?

beats.title: Ideas, more than time
beats.notes: Why did I build it? I usually have far more ideas than videos.

beats.title: A video, planned
beats.notes: I write notes, sometimes even a full script. Then I plan a video to go with the script,

beats.title: Beat 5
beats.notes: and this is when it usually stops.

beats.title: No time
beats.notes: Recording, drawing, editing, publishing: between my work and family, I never have enough time to do it.

beats.title: What if the board drew itself?
beats.notes: So the question became: what if the board could draw itself, and a model could help me do it?

elements.text:
my own dedicated
video creation assistant?

beats.title: A dedicated assistant
beats.notes: What if I could have my own dedicated video creation assistant? As you would have guessed, I gave it a try.

elements.text:
when you publish often,
keeping a consistent style matters

beats.title: Consistency matters
beats.notes: I started from basics: I defined the style.

beats.title: The reference
beats.notes: I took inspiration from IBM lightboard explainers. I enjoyed their aesthetics: a glass board and neon diagrams.

elements.text: a topic, a script, or a recording of me talking
every step on screen: asked, answered, checked
a first draft to react to

beats.title: One box
beats.notes: So where does a video start? With one box, and one sentence about what I want to explain.

beats.title: A sentence
beats.notes: Here I'm asking for an explainer about this very app: how one sentence becomes a video.

beats.title: Three ways in
beats.notes: That sentence is a topic. I could paste a script I've already written instead, or upload a recording of me talking it through, and every beat gets cued to the moment I say it.

beats.title: Watch it work
beats.notes: The model I picked writes it, and every step is on screen: what was asked, what came back, and what the checker found.

beats.title: A first draft
beats.notes: A minute later there's a first draft: scenes, drawings, beats and speaker notes. Not finished, but something to react to, and that's the hard part done.

elements.text: one window, built like a whiteboard
click anything: its properties open on the right
each card is one click, its actions in order
pick from the library: drawn in the same markers
P switches to Play, right where I am

beats.title: The editor
beats.notes: The draft opens in the editor. It's built to feel like a whiteboard, not like a video timeline.

beats.title: Click to select
beats.notes: I click anything on the board, and its properties open on the right: where it sits, how big it is, which marker draws it.

beats.title: The beats
beats.notes: Under the board are the beats. Each card is one click when I present, and its actions play in order, left to right.

beats.title: From the library
beats.notes: On the left are the scenes, and under them the library. I pick an icon, and it lands on the board, drawn in the same marker style as everything else.

beats.title: P to play
beats.notes: And when I want to see it move, P switches to Play, right where I am.

elements.text: a real recording, one frame per step
one click: its marker is lifted on the right
another marker: redrawn in that ink
recorded by the app, kept in the media library

beats.title: A real recording
beats.notes: Now a closer look at editing. This is a real recording of the app, and I'm stepping through it one frame at a time, in step with what I say.

beats.title: Select
beats.notes: One click selects the headline, and its properties open on the right, with the marker it's drawn in lifted up.

beats.title: Recolour
beats.notes: Pick another marker, and the text is redrawn in that ink. Yellow. Or pink.

beats.title: Rewrite
beats.notes: A double-click opens the text right where it is. I type the new words, press Enter, and they're written in the same hand.

beats.title: Made by the app
beats.notes: And this clip was made by the app itself: a short script clicks through the editor, and the recording lands in the media library, sharp enough to zoom into.

beats.title: LLM first
beats.notes: Under the hood, jz-motion is designed to be LLM first. A presentation is not pixels: it's simply a JSON document.

beats.title: Context
beats.notes: Every request sends the model the format reference, the drawing rules and the whole library: every icon, logo, clipart and 3D model it may use. So in reality, the LLM generates pure JSON.

beats.title: Schema check
beats.notes: The JSON is then sent to a schema checker, to make sure the result is correct.

beats.title: Repair
beats.notes: And if anything goes wrong, the exact errors go back to the model to fix.

beats.title: Board
beats.notes: Only valid JSON reaches the board, and from there it's all deterministic drawing.

beats.title: The JSON
beats.notes: Because it's plain JSON, I can read it, diff it, keep it in Git or edit it by hand.

elements.text: an ordinary screenshot: soft once the camera moves in
captured twice as large, the text a little bigger
select a recording, step through its frames
or drag straight to a moment
a beat goes to that frame

beats.title: Screenshots
beats.notes: Early on, I showed the app with ordinary screenshots. They looked fine, until the camera moved in.

beats.title: Captured larger
beats.notes: So now every capture is made twice as large, with the text a little bigger. The same zoom stays sharp.

beats.title: Frame by frame
beats.notes: Screen recordings are made the same way. When I select one on the board, I can step through it, frame by frame.

beats.title: Pick a moment
beats.notes: Or I drag straight to the moment I want to talk about.

beats.title: A beat goes there
beats.notes: Then one click, and a beat goes to that frame. That's how the demos in this video keep pace with what I say.

elements.text: my own takes, on the timeline
its wave, and how loud it is
play a part in a loop, or cut it out
the gain set until my voice sits in the green
record it again, or generate it again
my voice, copied from a sample I read once
the same voice, a softer accent

beats.title: Short takes
beats.notes: The voice took the longest to get right. At first, I recorded myself in short takes, straight onto the timeline.

beats.title: A closer look
beats.notes: Double-clicking a take opens it up: its wave, and how loud it is next to the level the video aims for.

beats.title: Fix a part
beats.notes: I can select a part, play it in a loop, or cut it out, with or without closing the gap.

beats.title: The microphone
beats.notes: Before recording again, I check the microphone, and turn the gain until my voice sits in the green.

beats.title: Record or generate
beats.notes: Then I either record the take again, or let the app say it for me, from the very same lines.

beats.title: My cloned voice
beats.notes: Generating only got good once it used my own voice. A cloning model copies it from a thirty-second sample I read once.

beats.title: A softer accent
beats.notes: It can even soften my accent. That's the version you're hearing now.

elements.text: six marker colours · one stroke · drawn in order

beats.title: Same markers
beats.notes: The other goal is consistency: whatever a model makes has to look like it came from the same set of markers.

beats.title: Everything
beats.notes: Icons, clipart, isometric 3D, charts, text.

beats.title: Six marker colours
beats.notes: The same six colours, the same stroke, drawn in the order a person would draw them.

beats.title: Make your own
beats.notes: When the library doesn't have something, I describe it, and the model draws it under the same rules.

beats.title: Versions
beats.notes: The rules are shown, and every reply is checked.

elements.text:
one source of truth —
so the house style stays the same

beats.title: One folder of skills
beats.notes: The skills folder is where I keep the rules: how to make a presentation, how to change one, how to draw a library item, how to demo an interface, or even how to turn it into a video.

beats.title: Both AIs follow them
beats.notes: The AI inside the app reads these files. Claude Code outside the app reads them too.

beats.title: One source of truth
beats.notes: So whichever one writes a scene, the style stays the same.

scenes.title: A library that lowers the cost

beats.title: A shelf of pieces
beats.notes: The library is the shelf of pieces every explainer draws from: icons, logos, hand-drawn clipart, 3D models, every one checked against the house style.

beats.title: Each explainer adds one
beats.notes: Reusing is free; generating new items costs tokens.

beats.title: So each one costs less
beats.notes: More in the library means fewer new items each time, and every explainer costs less than the one before.

beats.title: Overview
beats.notes: Here's how it fits together.

beats.title: In the browser
beats.notes: In the browser, we have a frontend application made with React. SVG animations are made with GSAP, and 3D coordinates are calculated with Three.js.

beats.title: A small local server
beats.notes: It's paired with a local server responsible for keeping the files, proxying LLM calls, transcription of recordings and export of videos.

beats.title: Swappable models
beats.notes: To generate presentations, I'm using either my local subscription or OpenRouter.

scenes.title: The right model for each job

beats.title: Right job
beats.notes: Because every request is checked and repaired, I can experiment with smaller models.

beats.title: Story
beats.notes: I'm using the most capable models for writing the story: the structure, the scenes, the words.

beats.title: Small edits
beats.notes: Small edits, like changing a beat, work fine with fast, cheap models like Haiku.

beats.title: Drawings
beats.notes: Thanks to well-defined skills, I'm also using Haiku for icons, charts and 3D models.

beats.title: Voice
beats.notes: For transcription I use a small OpenAI model. At first I recorded the voice-over myself, but as I kept updating the script, I switched to AI: a clone of my own voice, so a changed sentence doesn't mean recording it again.

elements.text:
I work on the words
independently from the board —
the board follows what I write.

beats.title: Script at the centre
beats.notes: The script is at the centre of this application. Every scene, every beat, every spoken sentence lives in one place.

beats.title: Three ways to touch it
beats.notes: I can read and edit the whole thing in the Script view, inline in the Timing prompter,

beats.title: Same text, three lenses
beats.notes: or in the raw JSON tab if I want to see the shape.

elements.text: Timing opens on the scene I was working on
one sentence per line, with the time it should take
my voice on two lanes, every beat placed on it
Record, read, → for the next line
clean up the voice, or get the words back

beats.title: Timing
beats.notes: When the words are right, I open Timing. It starts on the scene I was working on, and the script turns into a prompter.

beats.title: One line at a time
beats.notes: Each sentence sits on its own line, large enough to read from across the room, with the time it should take beside it.

beats.title: The timeline
beats.notes: Underneath is the timeline: my voice on two lanes, and every beat placed on it. Drag a beat, and that's the moment it appears in the video.

beats.title: Just read
beats.notes: To record, I press Record and read. The arrow key moves on to the next line, and every beat lands exactly where I said it.

beats.title: Tidy up
beats.notes: If a take is noisy, one click cleans up the voice. If I want the words back, it transcribes them for me.

elements.text: not one button in the corner
home: one sentence, a first draft
the scene bar: change just this scene
the AI tab: bigger changes, each step shown
the library: describe the picture you need
the same skills everywhere, so it all looks like it belongs

beats.title: Everywhere
beats.notes: The AI isn't one button in the corner. It's wherever I happen to be working.

beats.title: Home
beats.notes: On the home screen, it turns a sentence into a first draft.

beats.title: This scene
beats.notes: In the editor, the bar above the beats changes just this scene: split a beat, add a database, or, like here, turn one part into a scene of its own.

beats.title: The AI tab
beats.notes: The AI tab is for bigger conversations about the whole presentation, and I can watch each step as it edits the file.

beats.title: The library
beats.notes: And in the library, I describe a picture I'm missing, and it's drawn in the same marker style.

beats.title: Same skills
beats.notes: Every one of them reads the same skills, so whichever I reach for, the result looks like it belongs.

elements.text: for a 10-minute video, start to finish

beats.title: The number
beats.notes: One of my main goals was to create an app that would let me make a ten-minute explainer video for under five dollars. I'm happy to share that I was successful.

beats.title: Why it works
beats.notes: If I had to name three main contributors to that success: a presentation is pure JSON, so tokens are cheap;

beats.title: Beat 3
beats.notes: the library grows, so most drawings are reused;

beats.title: Beat 4
beats.notes: and the repair loop lets me use small, fast models.

beats.title: Record
beats.notes: And now the last mile: I click Record and adjust the timing, like I'm doing right now.

beats.title: Export
beats.notes: My script, my voice and every click are saved as a take.

beats.title: Thanks
beats.notes: Thank you for watching.
